generator.source: tpAgent.tools() via core scripts/agent-tool-catalog.cjs, mapped by tools/agent/src/catalog.js

instructions:
You are building in the person's own open theprototype.app tab: a live, shared 3D scene. Every change shows for everyone in the session and can be undone.
This may be a VOICE conversation: answer in one or two short spoken sentences and say what changed in plain words ("Added three trees by the fire"). Never read out uuids, lists of numbers or JSON.
If a tool says the tab is closed or not connected, tell the person to open theprototype.app and press Connect Claude, then wait; do not retry in a loop.
Call status first: it says whether you may edit (a viewer can only look).
Call list_scene before editing so you use real uuids; batch many objects into one call.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.
Use screenshot to check a result when it matters, not after every step.
When asked what you can do here, call what_can_you_do and say its "say" line.

tools.name: list_scene
tools.description: List every object currently in the scene with its uuid, name, type, parent, transform, material and color. Call this before editing so you use real uuids. A big flow graph shows its first page and says how to read the rest: pass {flow: "scene" | object uuid, page} to read one page of one graph.

flow.description: optional: read one flow graph ("scene" or an object uuid) page by page instead of the scene summary

tools.name: create_objects
tools.description: Create one or more primitives, lights or empty groups in a single call. Ground is the y=0 plane; place objects so they rest ON it (a box of height h sits at y=h/2). Returns the new uuids.

params.description: up to 4 constructor args. Box=[w,h,d], Sphere=[radius], Cylinder=[rTop,rBottom,height], Cone=[radius,height], Plane=[w,h], Torus=[radius,tube]. Omit for sensible defaults.

color.description: hex like #ff8800 (a mesh, or a light's colour)

intensity.description: lights: brightness (point/spot also fall off with distance)

aim.description: directional/spot: a world point [x,y,z] to point at

parentUuid.description: uuid of an existing group to nest under

physics.description: default static (it stays put in Play). dynamic = it falls, collides and can be thrown — only when asked for

tools.name: update_objects
tools.description: Modify existing objects by uuid: move/rotate/scale, recolor, change material, rename, show/hide, or reparent. Batch many in one call.

materialParams.description: meshes: numbers (roughness, metalness, opacity, emissiveIntensity, clearcoat, transmission, ior, shininess…, clamped), true/false (wireframe, transparent, flatShading), hex colours (emissive, specular), side (front|back|double), and map = a library image hash (null clears). Each bad key comes back in errors.

intensity.description: lights: brightness (point/spot also fall off with distance)

aim.description: directional/spot: a world point [x,y,z] to point at

parentUuid.description: group uuid to nest under, or "root" to un-nest

tools.name: delete_objects
tools.description: Delete objects by uuid.

tools.name: group_objects
tools.description: Create a new group and move the given member objects into it. Returns the group uuid.

tools.name: clear_scene
tools.description: Delete ALL objects in the scene. Requires confirm:true. Use only when the user clearly asks to start over.

tools.name: create_flow_nodes
tools.description: Add behavior (flow) nodes to a node graph — this is how objects get MOTION and interactivity: spin, bounce, patrol a path, pulse, blink, react to clicks. graph is "scene" or an object uuid (ONE graph per call). KEY RULE: a behavior node placed in an OBJECT's graph with no edges automatically drives that object — most behaviors are one node, zero edges, so usually OMIT edges. Describe nodes EITHER as text (graph lines, see the system prompt) OR as nodes/edges arrays. A call with some bad nodes still creates the good ones and returns partial:true + errors[] — resend only what errors[] names.

graph.description: "scene" or an existing object uuid (nodes in an object's graph drive that object)

text.description: graph lines: `ref = type "label" {params}` per new node (omitted params = defaults), `ref.out -> other.in` per wire (refs or existing node ids). e.g. "c = onclick\nl = latch {initial: false}\nc -> l.set"

ref.description: local key so edges in THIS call can reference the new node

type.description: a node type from the system prompt's Node types

data.description: node params, e.g. spin {axis:"y",speed:2}; bounce {amplitude:0.5,speed:2}; pathpatrol {points:[[x,y,z],…] (>=2 world waypoints), speed:1, mode:"loop"|"pingpong"}; setcolor {color:"#ff0000"}; latch {initial:false}; delay {seconds:3}; sequence {delay1:0,delay2:0.5,delay3:0.5,delay4:0.5} (delays are CUMULATIVE). Omit for defaults.

edges.description: optional wires between nodes (by ref or existing node id). Usually OMIT — unwired behavior nodes already drive their graph's object.

tools.name: update_flow_nodes
tools.description: Tune or remove existing behavior nodes in one graph. Node ids and current data are in the scene summary under each object's "flow" (and "sceneFlow").

tools.name: describe_node_types
tools.description: Look up flow node types before wiring them: per type its inputs (toHandle names + socket types), its output type and named outputs (fromHandle), its params with types and defaults, and one line on what it does. No arguments = every type name by group; group = that group with one-line docs; types = full details (up to 12). Changes nothing.

tools.name: create_behaviour

target.description: "scene" (default) or an object uuid the behaviour belongs to

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: edit_behaviour
tools.description: Replace an existing behaviour's source (the scene summary lists them; read the current source with the name). Linted before it is applied. Same format as create_behaviour (see its description).

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: set_physics
tools.description: Set physics body params on objects (batch). NOTE: objects made with create_objects are STATIC unless created with physics "dynamic" or a mass — use this to make existing objects dynamic, to TUNE bodies, or to pin scenery (mode "static"). mode "auto" reverts to scenery defaults.

collider.description: trimesh = the exact mesh, for static scenery (tunnels, pools, arches); a dynamic body gets its hull

sensor.description: true = a trigger volume: no collision response, fires On Enter/On Exit nodes

group.description: collision group; water = a pass-through trigger volume

collidesWith.description: groups this object collides with (omit = all); leave out player for a ghost wall the player walks through

tools.name: create_joints
tools.description: Attach object pairs with physics joints: "fixed" welds them rigidly, "revolute" hinges around an axis (optional motor spins it). Move parts to their final pose WORLD-ALIGNED (no rotation) before jointing. Without anchor a hinge sits at b's origin (its centre) and a weld midway: pass anchor [x,y,z] (world) for the real pivot, e.g. the top of a pendulum rod or a door's edge. Jointed bodies that touch (a door in its frame, a wheel in its arch) also need contacts:false, or the solver pushes them apart.

b.description: uuid of the attached object (hinge anchors at its origin)

anchor.description: world [x,y,z] of the pivot/weld point (default: b's origin for a hinge, midway for a weld)

contacts.description: false = the two bodies stop colliding with each other (default true)

limits.description: revolute only: [min, max] radians the hinge may turn

tools.name: control_simulation
tools.description: Start, stop, pause, resume or reset the physics simulation. After building a physics assembly, start the simulation so the user sees it move.

tools.name: install_modules
tools.description: Install the modules the other peers in this session run and this page lacks (status().missingModules), from the module gallery. Local to this page; omit ids to install every missing one.

ids.description: module ids; omit for all missing

tools.name: pending_offers
tools.description: List the questions the app is asking this page (an admin-role offer, "share or stash your scene"…), each with its buttons. Answer one with accept_offer.

tools.name: accept_offer
tools.description: Press a button on a pending offer (see pending_offers). action = the button label; omit for the first button.

tools.name: what_can_you_do
tools.description: Answer "what can you do here?": a short spoken summary of what you can build in this tab, what you cannot do, and example requests. Changes nothing.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Join a theprototype.app session. Pass the link the host shared (https://theprototype.app/#F0FD3, possibly with &invite=…) or the bare session id. An invite link joins at once; a plain link asks the host to Approve. The scene tools appear once the agent page is up; call status to see whether you are in.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Where the agent is: connection state, whether the host has let it in, its role (viewer edits stay local), the app version, and why any tool is missing.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: See the scene: a PNG of a clean frame (no gizmos) from a temporary camera, never moving anyone's view. view: current | top | front | iso | focus (focus needs uuid).

tools.name: wait_for_edit
tools.description: Wait until someone in the session changes the scene (or the timeout passes), so you can react to the humans.
